title: Binary compatibility scoring + temporary quarantine lane for customer-submitted model variants
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a product playbook and lightweight automation to accept customer-requested model variants into a temporary quarantine lane. The lane applies a binary-compatibility score against the customer's current pinned model and enforces automated eval gates (semantic drift, hallucination regression, latency and cost delta, PII leakage signals). Successful candidates can be auto-promoted or routed to human review; failing candidates are rejected with actionable feedback. Goal: reduce manual triage time for enterprise requests while preserving stability for pinned workloads.
background: Enterprise customers frequently request new model variants or version pins for compatibility or performance. Current intake is manual and conservative: many safe upgrades are delayed due to lack of a fast, auditable compatibility check. Recent incidents where a poorly vetted variant increased hallucination rates highlighted the need for a gated fast-path that balances speed with safety and auditability.
proposed_solution: Create a 'quarantine' intake lane in the catalog intake workflow that: 1) automatically runs a binary-compatibility scorer comparing candidate variant outputs to the customer's pinned model over a standardized prompt suite; 2) executes automated eval gates with configurable thresholds per customer tier; 3) surfaces diffs and metrics in Console and the intake ticket; 4) supports auto-promotion to staging/dedicated if thresholds met or escalates to review when borderline. Provide templated feedback to customers when variants fail gates and an appeal path.
acceptance_criteria: Quarantine lane available in intake UI with option to select 'compatibility check' for customer-submitted variants
Automated compatibility score computed and attached to the ticket within 1 hour for standard prompt suites

Eval gates implemented: semantic-similarity (>=0.92), hallucination delta (<=+2%), latency delta (<=+20%), cost delta (<=+10%), PII detection (0 new flags), with thresholds configurable per enterprise tier
Console shows per-variant diff dashboard and a downloadable report for audits
Auto-promotion flow triggers when all gates pass and owner approved; audit log entries recorded for promotion events
Customers receive templated failure reports that include example prompts, failing outputs, and suggested mitigations
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design & review (2 weeks) - PM, Eng, Research, Security align on scorer and gate set
Phase 1: Internal pilot with 3 strategic customers (4 weeks) - use sandbox prompt suites and manual oversight
Phase 2: Automation & Console integration (3 weeks) - CI for running prompt suites, attach reports to tickets
Phase 3: Wider beta & threshold tuning (4 weeks) - gather metrics, tune thresholds and tier defaults
Phase 4: GA and doc playbook (2 weeks) - publish intake playbook, support templates, update runbooks
metrics: Time-to-first-decision for enterprise variant requests (goal: reduce from median 7 days to <48 hours)
% of successful auto-promotions vs manual escalations
Post-promotion regression rate for hallucination/PII incidents (target: no increase)
Customer satisfaction score on intake experience (NPS-like question)
False-reject rate (variants rejected but later accepted after appeal)
tradeoffs: Risk of false negatives (unsafe variants promoted) vs faster time-to-decision; mitigated by conservative default thresholds and human-in-loop for high-risk customers
Engineering cost to maintain per-customer prompt suites and running compute for automated evaluations
Potential increase in audit and compliance workload due to additional reports; we mitigate by templating and retention policies
